s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of a painless swelling over a pacemaker site with persistent systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Painless swelling over the pacemaker site
Persistent fatigue, dyspnea, and cough after COVID-19 infection
Soft tissue mass with increased vascularity surrounding the device on chest ultrasound
key_facts: 70-year-old man with a history of nicotine use
Remote history of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
Remote history of bladder urothelial carcinoma
Dual-chamber pacemaker implantation for sick sinus syndrome 9 months prior
Normal pacemaker function and clinically unremarkable pocket at postoperative checks
Tested positive for COVID-19 infection three weeks before presentation
Fatigue, dyspnea, and cough persisted and worsened after COVID-19 infection
New swelling over the pacemaker site reported at a routine cardiology visit
Normal blood pressure and heart rate on examination
No signs of cardiac decompensation or cachexia
Chest ultrasound revealed a soft tissue mass with increased vascularity surrounding the device
CT imaging confirmed a soft-tissue mass around the pacemaker pocket
Haematoma or infection was excluded

shortlist.label: Metastatic disease
shortlist.why_kept: History of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma and bladder urothelial carcinoma with new swelling over pacemaker site

shortlist.label: Pacemaker pocket tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Painless swelling over pacemaker site with increased vascularity on ultrasound and soft tissue mass on CT imaging

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid growth and increased vascularity of the soft tissue mass surrounding the pacemaker

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic symptoms such as fatigue, dyspnea, and cough with a new swelling over the pacemaker site

shortlist.label: Sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Soft tissue mass with increased vascularity surrounding the pacemaker, a possible sign of malignant tumor growth

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of cancer and presented with a soft tissue mass surrounding the pacemaker device, which was confirmed by chest ultrasound and CT imaging, with haematoma or infection excluded.

rejected.label: Metastatic disease
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of cancer, the presence of a localized mass around the pacemaker site suggests a primary tumor at the site rather than metastasis.

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence provided to suggest angiosarcoma, such as rapid growth or metastasis, which are common with this aggressive tumor type.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Lymphoma would more likely present with systemic symptoms and lymphadenopathy rather than a localized mass around a pacemaker site.

rejected.label: Sarcoma
rejected.why: While sarcoma is a broad category of tumors, the specific context of a mass around a pacemaker site, especially in a patient with a history of cancer, suggests a pacemaker pocket tumor as a more direct explanation.
